title: Celine Dion Sings Again After Rare Illness!
summary:
Have you ever promised to do something and then worked really hard to keep that promise? Celine Dion did. After nearly four years away from the stage, the famous singer returned to Paris on Saturday, September 12, 2026, for her 16-show residency at the Plenitude Arena.

Dion has a rare condition called stiff person syndrome. It causes stiff limbs and severe muscle spasms. It can make walking difficult and even stop her from using her vocal cords to sing the way she used to. She announced her diagnosis in 2022.

But on Saturday, she opened the show with the French song 'On Ne Change Pas,' which means 'we don't change.' After finishing, she had tears in her eyes. 'I had promised myself not to cry,' she told the crowd. 'Thank you so very much for coming. ... I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. So here I am, singing for you and singing for me, singing live!'

Videos show her in a black dress with her hair in a bun, singing hits like 'Because You Loved Me' and 'Power of Love.' She also sang 'My Heart Will Go On' from the movie Titanic. A few hours before the show, she posted a smiling photo on Instagram with the caption 'En route!' (on the way!).

Dion is from Quebec, a French-speaking part of Canada, and she is deeply loved in France. Her concerts are sold out and are expected to bring in millions of dollars for the region. Her last tour was interrupted in 2020 by the COVID-19 pandemic, and she performed at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony in July 2024. Now she's back, and fans are thrilled.
why_it_matters: Dion's comeback shows that people with health problems can still work toward big goals with time and help, and it reminds us to be kind to classmates or family members who are sick.

Her song 'My Heart Will Go On' comes from the movie Titanic, and it is one of the most famous movie songs ever recorded.

Stiff person syndrome is a real medical condition that affects the nerves that control muscles, and doctors treat it with special medicines and gentle exercise; Dion also sang at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony in 2024, where the world's biggest sports event is held every four years.
